## How this work is cited

Passages inside Renjian Cihua are identified by numbered item (則). The corpus cites the work under its romanised title and under an English rendering on different pages. They are the same text, and the numbered item is what identifies a passage in it.

## The work in Wang Guowei’s thought

Wang Guowei (1877–1927) was a late Qing–Republican scholar who joined classical Chinese learning with Western aesthetics and philosophy. He wrote on tragedy, ci poetry, oracle bones, and the history of Song–Yuan drama. [More on Wang Guowei](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-guowei) .

1.  > Those who in ancient or modern times achieved great enterprises and profound learning must pass through three realms: first, standing alone atop a high tower after the west wind withers the green trees, gazing to the end of the road at heaven's edge; second, the belt growing looser without regret, wasting away for the beloved; third, searching a thousand times in the crowd, then suddenly turning — and finding that person standing where the lanterns grow sparse.
    
    [Wang Guowei: “Those who in ancient or modern times achieved…” — source & context](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0174)
    
2.  > In the realm with a self, one views things through the self, so things take on one’s coloring. In the realm without a self, one views things through things, and no longer knows which is self and which is thing.
    
    [Wang Guowei: “In the realm with a self, one views…” — source & context](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0482)
    
3.  > Ci poetry takes jingjie — the aesthetic realm — as its highest: with jingjie it naturally attains a lofty style and famous lines of its own.
    
    [Wang Guowei: “Ci poetry takes jingjie — the aesthetic realm…” — source & context](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0688)
    
4.  > Jingjie is not a matter of scenery alone: joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness are also realms of the human heart. Whoever can write true scenery and true feeling may be said to have jingjie.
    
    [Wang Guowei: “Jingjie is not a matter of scenery alone:…” — source & context](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes/q0689)
